lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Use one standard for date dashes and spacing throughout.
items.because: The dates are generally consistent, but the formatting should be uniform.

items.says: Format wrapped bullets so their continuation is visually clear.
items.because: Bullets split after words such as “intercompany,” “request,” and “more than 5%” may wrap awkwardly.

items.says: Consider a short professional summary if targeting a specific role.
items.because: The résumé does not indicate whether the target is corporate finance, FP&A, valuation, or credit.

items.says: Prioritize relevant achievements if the résumé is intended to be one page.
items.because: With five years of experience, weak or redundant bullets should not be kept simply to fill space.

items.says: Consider moving the Student Investment Fund out of Projects if it was a university organization.
items.because: Its placement should reflect whether it was an activity, leadership experience, or project.

items.says: Explain the current move from financial analyst to caddie or make the role’s relevance clearer.
items.because: Listed first as the current role, it may look like an unexplained step backward and distract recruiters from the finance experience.

items.says: Verify or replace the LinkedIn URL.
items.because: “example.com/in/rchen” looks like placeholder text.

items.says: Remove the example.com link if it is not an actual site.
items.because: A portfolio or project link is useful only if it is real and useful.

items.says: Consider adding strong, relevant coursework, honors, GPA, or finance activities.
items.because: Routine academic details from a 2020 degree would not strengthen the candidacy.

items.says: Replace the vague frequency and task description with evidence of scale, service, responsibility, or performance.
items.because: “About 5 rounds a week” says little about your value.

items.says: Give “carrying bags” a clearer purpose or leave it out.
items.because: It is an expected duty unless it demonstrates reliability, physical demands, customer service, or work during a transition.

items.says: Clarify the members served, work volume, service responsibilities, or trust-based duties if accurate.
Specify what operational responsibility “helped” means.
items.because: The verb does not show whether you handled registration, scheduling, scoring, communication, or logistics.

items.says: Add the tournament’s scale if available.
items.because: Participant numbers, event frequency, or operation size would give the coordination work more detail.

items.says: Define and substantiate the 40% improvement in “close efficiency.”
items.because: A baseline and measurement method, such as days or hours saved, are needed for credibility.

items.says: Explain what was automated and which tools were used, if relevant.
Confirm that “intercompany eliminations” describes the work and distinguish it from reconciliations if needed.
items.because: The processes or outcomes may have differed.

items.says: Add the capital plan’s business outcome if available.
items.because: Faster approvals, improved comparability, reduced review time, or expenditure managed would show its impact.

items.says: Clarify whether you built, owned, or merely used the NPV template.
Check whether “same discount rate” accurately reflects company policy.
items.because: Projects with different risk profiles may warrant different rates.

items.says: Specify what “more than 5% off budget” means.
items.because: The threshold could mean unfavorable variances, variances in either direction, or something else.

items.says: Identify what “each line” refers to.
items.because: It could mean business units, accounts, cost centers, or financial statement lines.

items.says: Add the scale of the variance commentary.
items.because: The number of entities, accounts, or reports covered would provide context.

items.says: Show decision support rather than only report preparation.
items.because: That would make the bullet stronger.

items.says: The FCFE and WACC valuation method is mismatched.
items.because: FCFE should generally be discounted at the cost of equity; WACC is normally used with unlevered free cash flow.

items.says: Clarify whether you performed the full valuation or supported one part of the deal analysis.
Add a disclosable transaction size, valuation range, or decision impact.
items.because: If the deal was confidential, the type of analysis and its use in the process can be emphasized instead.

items.says: Adding three unit EBITDA margins does not produce a valid group EBITDA margin.
items.because: A consolidated margin uses total EBITDA divided by total revenue, with appropriate weighting.

items.says: Remove or correct the 45% figure based on how the consolidated margin was calculated.
items.because: The number should not be retained merely because it sounds impressive if it is not correct.

items.says: The cash-flow achievement is duplicated in the Student Investment Fund entry.
items.because: The fund project predates Stonebridge, making it questionable which experience produced the result.

items.says: Clarify what the USD 600M describes.
items.because: It could refer to revenue, assets, debt, or company size.

items.says: Explain how the under-4% forecast error was measured.
items.because: It could mean absolute percentage error or variance to actual cash flow.

items.says: Qualify the forecast’s role in the debt repayment.
items.because: It may have helped treasury identify excess liquidity but probably did not independently cause the repayment.

items.says: Add a measurement date for the two-year default claim.
items.because: Some loans may not yet have reached two years of seasoning.

items.says: Define and confirm the population and default period behind “none defaulted.”
items.because: The absolute claim must cover the approved loans and a defensible period.

items.says: Consider how much of the default result is attributable to your underwriting.
items.because: It might instead reflect a small or favorable sample.

items.says: Clarify whether the declined applications were all applications or a sample.
Define the measurement window for “early defaults.”
Specify whether your findings changed the thresholds directly or informed a committee decision.
Give the period over which approvals rose, if specified.
items.because: The increase from 41% to 48% needs context.

items.says: “Writes” uses present tense for a role that ended in 2022.
items.because: Completed work in a previous role should use past tense.

items.says: Clarify whether you created, revised, or maintained the checklist.
State the portfolio size or number of borrowers monitored.
Explain how and over what period missed tests were counted.
Verify that the checklist drove the reduction in missed tests.
items.because: A broader process change may have contributed to the drop from seven to one.

items.says: Specify which credit memos saw the time reduction.
items.because: It may have applied to all memos, one loan segment, or a pilot group.

items.says: Identify the tools used if relevant to target roles.
Add any supportable improvement in consistency or errors.
items.because: The template may have delivered benefits beyond time saved.

items.says: Give the date used for the market-price comparison.
items.because: Proximity to market price depends heavily on the comparison date.

items.says: Explain what “within 6%” means and what conclusion it supports.
items.because: It does not say whether the model was above or below market or whether this was validation or an investment conclusion.

items.says: Describe the valuation methods and outputs without overstating accuracy.
items.because: Matching the market price does not necessarily mean the valuation was correct.

items.says: Distinguish completed work from ongoing work.
items.because: The project is dated “Present.”

items.says: Specify whether “1-point” means one percentage point.
items.because: It could otherwise be read as a one-percent relative change.

items.says: Explain the scenarios and whether other assumptions stayed constant.
Frame the sensitivity as an analytical result, not necessarily a business achievement.
Clarify whether you presented, answered questions, or contributed to the recommendation.
Add the approximate audience or club size if meaningful.
Add the year of the “spring pitch.”
items.because: The reference may become unclear over multiple recruiting cycles.

items.says: Avoid implying that the club validated the valuation by using the materials.
items.because: Use of the model and note alone does not establish validation.

items.says: Clarify the organization and team behind the FP&A work.
items.because: An FP&A team appears inconsistent with a student investment fund unless it was a separate organization or function.

items.says: Replace the generic reporting-and-analysis description with specific work or remove it.
items.because: The bullet does not say what reporting or analysis you performed.

items.says: Verify that this work is not being confused with Stonebridge work.
Identify the benchmark type and reporting frequency if relevant.
Specify whether you built, redesigned, automated, or improved the report’s accuracy.
Verify “every meeting” and consider quantifying the meetings or periods.
items.because: The phrase is broad.

items.says: The cash-forecast achievement duplicates Stonebridge’s and appears misassigned.
items.because: The same USD 600M, 4%, and USD 40M metrics appear in both roles, and the result seems implausible for a student investment fund.

items.says: If this was a separate project, explain its organization and business context.
items.because: Otherwise, it looks copied or misassigned.

items.says: Add proficiency levels only if meaningful and defensible.
List specific Excel capabilities you actually use if relevant.
items.because: Capabilities such as Power Query, VBA, or Power Pivot may be useful for target roles.

items.says: Show what Bloomberg Terminal was used for in an experience or project bullet.
items.because: That would make the listed tool stronger.

items.says: Add other tools only if you have genuine working experience with them.
Consider grouping valuation, corporate finance, and credit skills for different target roles.
items.because: The methods should be tailored without becoming a long keyword list.

items.says: Correct the FCFE/WACC issue before emphasizing DCF valuation as a skill.
items.because: The résumé currently contradicts the method technically.

items.says: Consider adding other methods central to the jobs being targeted.
items.because: Variance analysis, cash-flow management, capital budgeting, covenant analysis, or financial statement analysis may be relevant.
